As the leader of one of the 7 great cities of the ancient world, you must carefully gather resources, develop commercial routes, and affirm your military supremacy. You draft cards over multiple rounds, carefully building towards long-term goals. Build your city and erect an architectural wonder that will transcend time! During the game, you can also build and upgrade your wonder , which gives you additional advantages (points or capabilities). You do not need to construct your wonder at all, but it is recommended. The player with the most points at the end of the game wins ! Table setup Number of players: • it is possible to play with 3 to 7 players on BoardGameArena. • BoardGameArena suggests 4 players • BoardGameGeek community suggests 4-5 players. Choices: • Game mode : normal and training • Game speed : as any other game • Wonder board side : allow players to choose their preferred side of their Wonder board, or set it randomly Preparation If Wonder board side has been set to Choose Wonder side , at the very beginning the players can choose between two sides of their Wonder board. Side A is usually easier to accomplish. Gameplay The game proceeds over 3 ages , each comprising 6 rounds. Card drafting rounds A round is simple: you are shown a hand of cards, you take one of them and perform one action with it, then the hand is moved on to the next player (shown by the hands rotation arrow). All players do this at the same time. Each age starts with 7 cards in each hand. The last round happens when the player has two cards in the hand: one is selected, the other is discarded. For each card, there can be three to four actions that you can take, shown when you hover on the card: 1. Construct (arrow pointing to card thumbnails): Add the specific card to your capabilities, paying its associated cost if any. The cost is shown on the top left of the card; a symbol over it shows if you are allowed to do this move: • a red cross indicates that you don't have and can't gather the necessary resources to construct • a yellow check mark with a number indicates how much you have to pay your neighbors to gather the necessary resources. − You can only buy resources from a neighbor if they have that resource available. − You pay 2 coins per resource, unless you have acquired a yellow card allowing you to buy that resource from that neighbor for only 1 coin. • a green check mark shows that you can construct with your own resources only 2. Build wonder stage (arrow pointing to a layered pyramid): Use this card as a marker on the lower side of the Wonder board, gaining the shown advantages (e.g. victory points, or capabilities). The Wonder plan can only be deployed passing through the stages in order, from left to right. A symbol below the next stage you can build shows you if it's possible to build it or not, with the same convention as explained above for constructing a card; 3. [Rating: 1/10] While not really a 1...this is a joke entry.  I find this game mediocre at best.  The base game is a solvable system.  With more cards the game becomes crazy complex mathematically, but still suffers from the same reaction I had to the base game: you're not doing anything.  Every other game I play that has drafting, you're creating a hand or deck of cards to play out later.  This ultimately feels unfulfilling.

[Rating: 1/10] Agree with other criticisms. Same bad passing mechanism as in the Fairytale game. It destroys strategy, makes for bad AP (look at players to side, try to figure how to not give 3 players 3 cards they or their neighbor(s) can use) ,and is confusing. Your military can only affect neighbors- too bad the nation away from you is building a bigger VP army! And your goals change thoughout play. I dub thee: 7 Blunders.

[Rating: 1/10] I don't understand the hype around this game. Simple solatire with one tricky rule. Fine to play once or twice.

[Rating: 1/10] This game is a tableau-builder which uses an innovative draft and pass mechanism that keeps all players engaged at all times. And that is the only positive. It should honestly get a 2 or 3 rating, but due to sponsor deals, it's at least a thousand places ahead of where it belongs on the hit parade here, so I downvote as hard as I possibly can.  Before you start, setup is a nightmare, requiring specific cards to be stripped or added from each of three age-specific decks depending on the number of players. Heaven forfend somebody wants to back out or join in while you "haven't started yet"    On

[Rating: 1/10] a lot of my friends have this game and love to play it. i just think it is way to hard and not easy to pick up. the idea of the game is good but i just dont get it. no matter how many times people explain it to me i just dont like it even more. everytime i hear the name i cringe... i do like the rotating of the hands and thats it.

[Rating: 1/10] Combines lack of strategy with wasteful planning. Easy to win and easy to lose. Very unthematic, I felt no part of any nation while playing this game.
